steps.body: A big pile is easy in groups of ten. 47 is 4 full tens and 7 leftover ones: count 10, 20, 30, 40… 47.
steps.narration: A big pile is easy in groups of ten. Forty-seven is four full tens and seven leftover ones: count ten, twenty, thirty, forty, then forty-seven.

commonBuilds.feedback: That builds 74 — the digits swapped. 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones.
That's just 4 tens (40). Add the 7 leftover ones: 47.

predict.prompt: 47 and 74 — would they be built from the same blocks?

options.label: No — different rods AND different cubes
Yes — the same blocks either way

predict.reveal: Swapping the digits swaps the jobs: 47 is four rods and seven cubes, 74 is seven rods and four cubes. Same symbols, different number entirely.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents count pile.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for count pile must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines count pile.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 62 is 6 tens and 2 ones — the tens digit tells the number of tens.
Count by tens to 60, then 2 more: 6 tens, 2 ones.

commonErrors.feedback: 2 is the ONES. The tens digit — the first one — is 6.
That's the whole number. It's made of 6 tens (and 2 ones).

steps.body: The tens digit counts the ten-groups; the ones digit counts the leftovers. In 85: 8 tens, 5 ones.
steps.narration: The tens digit counts the ten-groups; the ones digit counts the leftovers. In eighty-five: eight tens, five ones.

steps.body: Match each number to its tens and ones.

widget.prompt: Match each number to its groups.

pairErrors.feedback: 85 has 8 tens and 5 ones. 5 tens 8 ones is 58.
58 has 5 tens and 8 ones. 8 tens 5 ones is 85.

widget.missFeedback: First digit = tens, second = ones: 85 is 8 and 5.
widget.successFeedback: Every number split into tens and ones!

explanationVariants: 85 has 5 leftover ones — the ones digit.
After 8 full tens, 5 are left over in 85.

widget.prompt: How many leftover ONES are in 85?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 is the number of TENS. The leftover ones — the last digit — is 5.
That's the whole number. The leftover ones are just 5.

explanationVariants: 6 tens (60) beats 5 tens and some ones (50-something) — more tens wins.
Compare the tens first: 6 tens is more than 5 tens, so 62 > 58.

options.label: 62 (6 tens)
options.feedback: Yes — 6 tens beats 5 tens, so 62 is bigger.

options.label: 58 (8 ones)
options.feedback: 8 ones looks big, but 62 has more TENS (6 vs 5). Tens decide first: 62 wins.

options.label: they're equal
options.feedback: 62 has 6 tens, 58 has 5 tens — not equal. 62 is bigger.

widget.prompt: A pile has 9 tens and 4 ones. What number is it?

commonErrors.feedback: That swapped them. 9 TENS and 4 ones is 94, not 49.
That added 9 + 4. Tens are groups of ten: 90 + 4 = 94.

takeaways: Group a pile into tens plus leftover ones.
More tens means a bigger number.
steps.teaser: next: one more, one less, ten more, ten less.

concept.body: Slow down. 23 is 2 tens and 3 ones. Count the tens: 10, 20. Then 3 more ones: 23.
concept.narration: Slow down. Twenty-three is two tens and three ones. Count the tens: ten, twenty. Then three more ones: twenty-three.

explanationVariants: Count by tens to 20: that's 2 tens in 23.

commonErrors.feedback: 3 is the ones. The tens digit — the first one — is 2.
That's the whole number. It has 2 tens.
